baseline.validation: API tests: 479 passed, 2 skipped. Complete server suite: 10143 passed, 86 skipped, zero failures/errors, including five block mechanics regressions. Clean patch reapplication, JAR generation and distribution checks passed with BUILD_NUMBER=12. A parallel local test attempt exhausted native memory; the complete repeat with --max-workers=1 and ActiveProcessorCount=2 passed. No server startup, production deployment or benchmark.
baseline.scope: Active DivineMC features and supporting sources. Historical removed patches are reference only. Existing Leaf implementations take precedence over duplicate ports.
baseline.copyright: Original patch authors and licenses are preserved.

decisions.reason: Retain Leaf's existing configurable vanilla profiler implementation: Profiler.get returns InactiveProfiler when disabled, server profiler activation is bypassed, and debug/perf commands and resource reload profiling already honor the same policy. Do not add a second switch with competing defaults.

The inherited SparklyPaper implementation already guards movement-distance calculations by Vec3 identity before distanceToSqr, including the current tracker paths. Preserve it instead of nesting another identical guard.
The same join-ticket proposal is already inherited. Keep its five-second ticket, join hook and explicit loading/simulation/keep-dimension flags; the DivineMC variant omits those flags.

Add cancellable player/dispenser bottle-fill events with mutable result items. Cover water, dragon breath, honey and water cauldrons. Move the source's incorrect empty-cauldron pouring hook to the water-cauldron glass-bottle interaction, before level changes or inventory mutations, so both the new event and the existing cauldron event can prevent consumption. Keep source defaults and use Paper's held-slot resync instead of full-container resync.

Native dispatch helpers provide detached copies of input/result items and centralize hand resync for cancellation or glass-bottle results. Nullable results are rejected at the API boundary; plugin result replacement and mutable result edits remain supported.

Keep the inherited Leaf entity movement and Connection changes. Port only the remaining unused PacketProcessor watchdog deque/counter instrumentation; current native, applied Paper and owned server sources do not consume its diagnostic accessors. Packet filtering, exception reporting, fatal Error propagation and shutdown rejection stay intact.

Reuse the already loaded chunk during the downward scan shared by endermen, cats and random-teleport consumables. Preserve captured tree-generation block states by using the world path during capture, and preserve world bounds/VOID_AIR before reading directly from the chunk. The original teleport validation, collision checks, plugin events and causes remain unchanged.

Preserve the opt-in bounded per-thread cache, scoped to each resolver/sampler instead of sharing results across samplers. Include Y in the key because 26.3 erosion sampling uses blockY. Unpackable coordinates bypass caching. Enforce capacities from 1 to 65536 even for runtime changes; capacities below 16 no longer disable eviction.

Keep the inherited Gale firework persistence option. Add only the missing opt-in snowball policy through DontSaveEntity, preserving the native shouldBeSaved removal/passenger rules and normal persistence by default.

Separate native RCON response lines. Move the existing Bukkit LF delimiter into the native source so plugin messages retain exactly their previous formatting instead of acquiring duplicate blank lines. Keep LF framing on every platform.
Optional MC-258859 correction recognizes slopes in both signs on both axes. Comparisons avoid Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) overflow. Disabled by default; only future terrain generation is affected.

Opt-in one-game-tick placement/neighbor updates reuse the native redstone/event path for all eight waxed/weathering bulb variants. Already queued ticks complete even if the configuration is subsequently disabled. Default remains immediate vanilla updates.

Power edges and triggered placement can schedule crafting after one game tick. Use a separate crafter option: the source defines crafter1gt but accidentally reads copperBulb1gt at both scheduling sites. All four option combinations are covered. Default remains four game ticks.

The opt-in flag prevents both natural and Purpur instant decay without freezing distance bookkeeping. Keep the inherited cached-direction helper and world setter/block-change hooks instead of the source's replacement loop. Instant decay reads the resulting world state, preserving reconnected leaves and plugin replacements. Random-tick eligibility stays native and event cancellation remains effective when decay is enabled.
Retain TintedPaper's own identity, build metadata and attribution. Replacing it with the source fork's branding is not a feature port.
The inherited API already has its own Timings removal patch covering the timing classes and the command/plugin-manager call sites. Keep that version instead of replaying duplicate deletions.
The same isParallelWorldTickingEnabled, getTickTimes and getAverageTickTime API signatures and defaults are already provided by the inherited Fish API patch. Keep the existing version.

The plugin/event context logging hooks are already provided by the inherited Pufferfish Sentry integration. Retain the existing version rather than duplicating the feature. The source's additional legacy enable-failure lifecycle change is separate from those logging hooks and remains under review.

Remove default bukkit:reload and bukkit:rl registrations from construction and clearCommands. Keep the public ReloadCommand class and its message constant for binary/source linkage, and retain CraftServer.reload lifecycle validation. The separate vanilla datapack reload can still register normally. Two API regressions cover initial/cleared maps, vanilla registration and legacy class linkage.
Bukkit Color implements Adventure TextColor without discarding its Bukkit alpha channel. DyeColor can provide RGB values and apply a text style.
Additive fluent setters, axis offsets, block centering and coordinate comparison. Centering floors negative coordinates; isSame intentionally ignores world and rotation, matching the source API.

Default methods delegate to the existing World sound APIs. Blocks use their center and BLOCKS category. Entities retain their identity as sound emitters and infer the category unless explicitly supplied.
API and CraftEntity implementation expose the native movement-affecting block separately from the optional collision support block, without scanning or loading blocks.

The proposed Math.min local remains inside the same per-position lambda. It neither hoists the calculation out of the lambda nor changes the generated terrain. No extra patch is needed for that textual refactor.

The source caches successful hasJoinedServer results by username and returns them for a later login challenge without fresh session validation. Do not import this authentication bypass; any replacement must validate every new challenge.

Precompute aquifer cell centers with reusable positional random sources, use a four-nearest min/max network with native tie order, and reuse the per-aquifer pressure-noise scalar. Retain Paper's floating-point threshold operations. Widen candidate keys to long to preserve all 32 index bits; preserve positional factory classes and custom subclass behavior rather than converting public classes to records. Reseeding preserves the native all-zero Xoroshiro state normalization. Despite its title, the source patch contains no Beardifier changes.
decisions.validation: Normal and AllFeatures suites passed. Four aquifer regressions cover a pre-port terrain/fluid-update golden checksum across 18 seed/factory/origin combinations, independent nearest-center ordering with ties and indices above 65535, random stream parity including zero seeds, and custom factories retaining lazy sampling and Paper call order. No gameplay or benchmark validation.

decisions.reason: Bound IOWorker pending writes using the source's soft/hard defaults (8192/32678). Enforce the hard threshold inside foreground writes on the existing single executor so background starvation cannot bypass it. Drain oldest entries through native runStore, retaining coalesced data, null deletions and successful/exceptional futures. Normalize invalid limits and stop on an empty queue. This affects IOWorker users such as RecreatingSimpleRegionStorage; normal Moonrise chunk saves bypass this map and are not claimed to have a global memory cap.
decisions.validation: Normal and AllFeatures suites passed. Four NBT regressions exercise foreground-only submission with background draining held, newest-data coalescing, FIFO/null deletion preservation, exceptional writes without lost futures, bounded extra background work, and zero/negative thresholds. Actual filesystem failure/upgrade behavior remains unverified.

decisions.reason: Retain the inherited Carpet-Fixes optimized biome-corner search, as requested for features with an existing base version. It already prunes candidates and additionally uses quart-offset lookup and Y-axis pruning. Its numeric bound and summation policy differ from DivineMC; this is a retained base variant, not a claim of bitwise equality between implementations.

The inherited Gale/Carpet-Fixes properDye table covers the same color combinations and fallback-to-parent behavior. Preserve its per-world switch and existing simpleRandom use instead of introducing a competing global switch or changing its random stream. Both versions intentionally bypass data-driven dye mixing only when their option is enabled.

The inherited Airplane/Gale implementation already removes cached descending, bottom and held-item state and reads those values from the live entity, with the same null/empty-context fallbacks and retained placement/fluid flags.

The inherited implementation already uses a per-chunk lightning countdown and retains the same thunder/rain/configuration guards. Keep its world simpleRandom initialization rather than allocating a new java.util.Random per chunk as DivineMC does. This records the existing algorithm, not vanilla weather-sequence equivalence.

The inherited Gale implementation already provides the per-tick and per-projectile load counters, unloaded-chunk lookup, configurable discard and movement-reset behavior. Retain its per-world configuration and explicit Bukkit removal cause. No new claim of parallel-world safety is made for the inherited static counters.

World ticking already records the elapsed level tick duration into 100-, 200- and 1200-sample windows. Keep the existing tickTimes1m name and the additional TPS-bar integration rather than adding a duplicate tickTimes60s window. The matching world metrics API is also already inherited.

Keep the inherited Gale/Leaf plain-ingredient matcher and Bukkit constructor flag. Port the missing isPlain guard so exact/predicate ingredients use the full matcher. Fix the inherited full matcher's per-type removal of all regular counts instead of one grid slot, predicate routing through the regular pool, stale predicate exact keys, and missing cleanup when a predicate throws; otherwise importing the guard would expose those failures for native recipes.
CraftShapelessRecipe already passes the inherited true Bukkit-origin flag to the native constructor. Retain that integration while adding the missing native complex-ingredient guard separately.

The inherited Gale/Velocity writers already pack the same 1-5 VarInt and 1-10 VarLong encodings into byte/short/medium/int operations, including negative values. Keep the existing branch ladder and original reference writers rather than replace it with DivineMC's byte-size switch.

Non-transferred logins asynchronously build the secondary server-data response through the existing Paper server-list ping event. Reuse Paper's async executor and its existing shutdown lifecycle. Check disconnect state before dispatch and again after plugin listeners, and skip only the optional secondary status if shutdown rejects scheduling. No world work is moved to a worker.

Share event response construction between primary server-list pings and secondary login MOTD delivery. A cancelled primary ping still disconnects its status connection; a cancelled secondary event only suppresses that response. Guard an absent cached status instead of dereferencing it. Six regressions cover plugin MOTD edits, cancellation, pre/post-listener disconnects, missing status and executor rejection.

This patch only removes the lifecycle guard that refers to the source-deleted ReloadCommand class. TintedPaper preserves that public class and removes only its default command registrations, so the guard remains valid and necessary; deleting it would weaken the existing Paper API contract.

Expose the source's player/vehicle speed and displacement allowance and lag-only player speed allowance. Keep both switches false by default to preserve the current fork's movement policy, rather than copying DivineMC's enabled defaults. Player allowances set the initial Paper fail-move event decision instead of skipping the event, so plugins can still reject or allow movement. Vehicle speed/displacement checks honor only the all-movement switch, matching the source. Collision, unloaded-chunk, finite-packet and game-rule checks retain their existing paths. No work moves between threads.

PaperPluginManagerImpl.useTimings already returns false through the inherited Timings removal patch. Preserve the existing implementation and retained no-op API compatibility class instead of deleting it.

compatibilityFixes.reason: The inherited collection optimization used EnumMap for MushroomBlockTexture cap faces, but several enum constants intentionally use null. Restore the pinned Paper HashMap so initialization, nullable face lookup and legacy material APIs keep working.

The full exact-choice matcher inherited from Paper removes every regular item of a type when one grid slot is routed to an exact ingredient; it also fails to clear predicate-derived exact keys. Reproduced with Bukkit-origin recipes before changing the fast-path guard. Preserve per-slot accounting, route predicate choices only through tested exact keys, clear actual exact keys and restore accounting in finally. The separate native failure is caused by the inherited Leaf/Gale fast path and is addressed by the DivineMC guard.

pendingReview: The legacy enable-failure adaptation remains under review. Bottle events and the compatible default reload-command removal are integrated.
